claim: exercisedb.dev's README advertises 11,000+ structured exercises.
It advertises 15,000+ videos.
It advertises 20,000+ images.
It advertises 5,000+ GIFs.

The exercisedb-api repository carries an AGPL-3.0 LICENSE file. (That the repository holds only README.md and LICENSE was established by a git clone on 2026-10-22: three commits, latest 401ef93 of 2025-11-25.)
The README labels its v2 playground for exploration only and not for production.
quote: These endpoints are for exploration only and not recommended for production integration

claim: The v2 sample record carries a videoUrl pointing at an .mp4 file.
The v2 sample record has an overview.
quote: "overview": "The Lever Pec Deck Fly is a strength-building exercise

claim: The v2 sample record has exerciseTips.
The v2 sample record has variations.
The v2 sample record has keywords.
The v2 sample record has relatedExerciseIds.
exercisedb.dev names muscles anatomically, e.g. Pectoralis Major Clavicular Head, in targetMuscles.
The v2 sample tags a gender for the demonstration.
exercisedb.dev's sample uses equipment labels like LEVERAGE MACHINE.

free-exercise-db's README calls it an "Open Public Domain Exercise Dataset", with 800+ exercises. (Our count of 876 exercises and 1,746 image paths was made by parsing dist/exercises.json on 2026-10-22; a count has no verbatim quote.)
quote: Open Public Domain Exercise Dataset in `JSON` format, 800+ exercises with a browsable public searchable frontend

claim: The combined dist/exercises.json we counted (876 records; 1,746 image paths, all .jpg). Quote shows the record shape the count was taken over.
Records conform to a JSON Schema in the repository.
quote: All exercises are stored as seperate `JSON` documents and conform to the following [JSON Schema](./schema.json)

claim: Every record has id, name, level, mechanic, equipment, primaryMuscles, secondaryMuscles, instructions, category and images (force is also present in every record in our count).
The README lists force, mechanic and equipment as incomplete in some files.
quote: The following fields are incomplete in _some_ `JSON` files and in such have had to allow `null` in [schema.json](./schema.json)

claim: The README notes a small number of duplicate images.
quote: There are also a small number of duplicate images eg.

claim: Muscles come from a fixed list of 17 values (the enum runs abdominals ... triceps).
IDs are strings built from the name, such as Alternate_Incline_Dumbbell_Curl.
You can fetch the combined JSON and images from raw GitHub URLs as the README describes, prefixing image paths with the exercises/ raw URL.
quote: prefix any of image path's contained in the `JSON` with `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuhonas/free-exercise-db/main/exercises/` to get a hosted version of the image

claim: You can clone the repo and use the JSON files and images locally.
quote: You can check the repo out and use the `JSON` files and images locally

claim: Makefile tasks rebuild the combined file and emit newline-delimited JSON for a PostgreSQL import.
quote: To combine all `JSON` files into [Newline Delimeted JSON](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JSON_streaming#Newline-delimited_JSON) suitable for import into PostgreSQL use the following make task

claim: Equipment labels in free-exercise-db include body only and e-z curl bar.
exercisedb.dev now presents itself as AscendAPI, previously ExerciseDB.
The free V1 tier is 1,500 exercises with 180p GIFs and needs no authentication.
quote: 1,500 exercises with 180p GIFs. No authentication required, just call the hosted API directly.

claim: The free V1 endpoint is oss.exercisedb.dev/api/v1/exercises.
Free V1 media is 180p GIFs only; 360p to 1080p images and GIFs are on the paid RapidAPI tier.
quote: The free tier includes 180p GIFs only . Multi-resolution images and GIFs (360p–1080p) are available on the paid RapidAPI tier .

claim: AscendAPI describes the whole V1 dataset as over 2,000 exercises, available as a free hosted tier and a paid RapidAPI tier.
quote: featuring over 2,000 structured exercises with rich metadata, images, and GIFs. Available as a free hosted tier and a paid RapidAPI tier with enhanced features.

claim: ExerciseDB V1 records carry bodyParts, targetMuscles and equipments arrays.
ExerciseDB V1's sample record lists targetMuscles such as pectorals.
AscendAPI describes ExerciseDB V2 as 11,000+ exercises, 15,000+ videos and 20,000+ images.
quote: A multipurpose exercise dataset with 11,000+ exercises, 15,000+ videos, and 20,000+ images

claim: ExerciseDB V2 gives each exercise an MP4 demonstration video.
quote: Each exercise includes an MP4 demonstration video for in-app playback.

claim: Both V2 tiers are accessed via RapidAPI, and free-tier media is watermarked.
quote: Both free and paid tiers are accessed via RapidAPI. The only difference is that free tier media is watermarked .

claim: The free Basic plan includes 2,000 requests a month.
The free Basic plan includes 200 exercises in the library.
AscendAPI's free plans are limited to 1,000 requests per hour per API key.
quote: All free plans include a limit of 1,000 requests per hour per API key.

claim: The README links separate terms of use, which we could not open.
